items.event_time_ist: FT report published ~10:15 AM IST, Oct 21, 2026 (alleged Israeli strike planned for the Oct 10 weekend)
items.source_name: Financial Times (carried via NewsBeep, NewsInIsrael, United with Israel, Balkan Business News); Jerusalem Post denial via JBizNews
items.summary: The Financial Times reported Wednesday Oct 21 (citing three people familiar) that Netanyahu had instructed the IDF to prepare a multi-day bombing campaign against Iran over the weekend of Oct 10, targeting nuclear facilities, regime targets and energy/civilian infrastructure on a larger scale than February's Operation Roaring Lion. The plan was called off after opposition from Trump, who did not want the war reignited before the Nov 3 US midterms; the Pentagon declined comment. The report adds that renewed Israeli-US strikes in coming weeks remain on the table ('either there will be a deal, or there will be an attack'). Two days earlier (Oct 19), Defense Secretary Hegseth made his unannounced visit to Israel and met Netanyahu. The Jerusalem Post, in its own reporting Wednesday, disputes the FT premise: its sources said the IDF was not planning such a strike and neither Netanyahu nor Defense Minister Katz had ordered it to prepare, speculating the leak was designed to influence Israel's Oct 27 elections by casting Netanyahu as having been stopped by Trump. The underlying claim therefore remains contested between the FT's and JPost's sources. (Thumbnail: verified Reuters Iran-crisis stock image, June 2026.)
items.title: FT: Trump blocked planned Israeli multi-day bombing campaign against Iran over Oct 10 weekend; JPost sources deny any such plan existed
